title: Farm economics stack
explanation: Poles' Folwark mechanic and Chinese farm bonuses both reshape how farm food is created and stored — the same economic object (Farms) is modified from two angles in team games.

title: Extra food at game start
explanation: Incas' team llama adds an early food source that compounds with civilizations that start with extra villagers or unusual early economy — more bodies and more food before the first farm.

title: Population pressure vs housing
explanation: Huns skip houses while Teutons' cheaper farms support a dense economy — less housing tax for the team while Teuton allies scale villager count on cheaper farms.

title: Archer production pipeline
explanation: Britons' faster archery ranges and Mayans' cheaper archers reduce the combined time and resource cost of mass archer production in team archer compositions.

title: Cavalry + camel answer
explanation: Franks bring cheap knights; Hindustanis add team Scout Cavalry-line bonus damage vs buildings — complementary cavalry roles in early aggression and siege support.

title: Monk discount chain
explanation: Byzantines heal faster and Hindustanis' Imperial Camel upgrade path often appears in monk-heavy lobbies — both civs skew toward sustained Castle-age fights where monk value spikes.

title: Full tech visibility + power spike timing
explanation: Vietnamese reveal enemy Town Centers at game start; Burgundians spike at specific upgrade timings. Knowing opponent location helps coordinate early pressure around Burgundian power windows.

title: Infantry supply chain
explanation: Slav team bonus (+5 pop for military buildings) and Goth cheaper infantry create more building space and cheaper flood units — classic infantry team synergy.
